title: Ambient auth cards and live toolcall UX strip for API onboarding
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a compact, horizontally-scrollable UX strip (series of micro-assets) illustrating an "ambient auth" approach for the SDK quickstart: a set of credential cards (API key, OAuth device flow, tokenless ephemeral session) plus a paired streaming code snippet and a live tool-calling interaction mock. Goal: reduce cognitive load in the quickstart by surfacing recommended auth options, inline trade-offs, and one-click try-it flows for streaming + tool calls.
acceptance_criteria: A set of 6 digestible micro-assets (PNG + SVG) sized for docs hero and mobile that demonstrate: API key card, device-code flow card, ephemeral token card, streaming console snippet, toolcall flow with tool selection, and error/fallback state
Design assets uploaded to Figma project 'SDK Quickstart - March 2025' with componentized cards and export-ready frames
One annotated screenshot used in the README quickstart (docs repo PR linked) and one animated GIF showing streaming + toolcall handshake
PM and Eng have signed off on wording for recommended defaults and fallback guidance (comments resolved)
Accessibility checklist completed: color contrast, alt copy, and keyboard-focus order documented
tasks: Workshop with PM and Runtime Eng to finalize recommended default auth (meet 2025-03-11)
Create Figma component library for 'ambient-auth-card' variants and export frames (designer)
Produce JS and Go streaming snippet variants that map to existing SDK surface (engineer to verify)
Record a 6s animated GIF demonstrating a streaming result and subsequent toolcall (design)
Open docs PR with new hero image and quickstart copy + link to animated GIF (docs-engineer)
Run a brief usability pass with two internal engineers and incorporate feedback
engineering_check: Runtime engineering confirmed API key and ephemeral token examples align with runtime-1.21 interface (comment 2025-03-12)
Batching and streaming guidance added to snippet comments to avoid cold-start mistakes
comments: 2025-03-11 - Liam Patel (PM): Workshop summary - agreed default order: API key (ease) -> Device code (recommended for user devices) -> Ephemeral token (security). PM asked for short 'when to use' microcopy on each card.

2025-03-13 - Jana Müller (Eng): Confirmed device-code sample uses /v1/device endpoint from runtime-1.21; minor snippet change requested to shelve token exchange until backend support is live. Added a reference GitHub gist.

notes: Design decision: use horizontal microstrip to allow readers to scan options left-to-right; callout badges for 'recommended' and 'secure' to help selection
Edge case: show explicit fallback when streaming errors due to token expiry; engaged infra to add telemetry event for token-expiry during try-it
Follow-up: consider bundling a tiny interactive sandbox in the docs (Phase 2) that can open ephemeral sessions directly from the card
